metadata.name: Benito Mussolini
metadata.description: Italian Fascist dictator who established a one-party state, pursued imperial expansion and directed a corporatist economy.
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 1925–1943; earlier writings are contextual only. Historical analogies to contemporary technologies are explicitly inferred, not claims that the subject answered a modern questionnaire. Coalition constraints and contradictions are identified by axis.

review.notes: Independently read all 240 answer rationales against exact wording and checked every axis brief and counterargument. Reopened the contemporary Einaudi account of corporative economic powers, the 1938 diplomatic record of racial measures, and the Lateran settlement. Retained the mixed public/private ownership assessment rather than deriving ownership from state direction. Verified Catholic establishment separately from personal religion, and retained nuanced Culture vs Nature responses reflecting both Fascist character formation and later hereditary exclusion. Corrected inferences that treated any controlled migration system as a universal sponsorship rule or a military alliance as a required common foreign policy. Revised precaution rationales to address substantial evidence rather than indefinite trials or zero risk. Modern technology positions are explicitly analogical, and racial attribution describes the subject’s claims rather than endorsing them.
